problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

- $¬X∧(X∨¬Y)$
- $¬X∨(X∧¬Y)$
- $¬(X∨(¬X∧Y))$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

- $¬(X∧¬Y)$
- $¬(X∨¬Y)$
- $¬X∧Y$
feedback.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,¬(X∧¬Y)\,$ | $\,¬(X∨¬Y)\,$ | $\,¬X∧Y\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

We see that only the statements $¬(X∨¬Y)$ and $¬X∧Y$ have the same truth table, so they are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".
